Loan matrix: each `NAME__conflict.rx` uses a view after a write, move or `&var` of a place it may denote, each `NAME__dead.rx` (and `__dead_conflict`, a Copy operand) does not, either because its last read comes first or because it denotes only other places; `NAME.expect` is the output a clean run prints. Names are `<shape>__<op>__<variant>`.

- `gen.py` writes every program (`python3 gen.py`); `gen.py --check` fails when the committed files differ from it. Edit the generator, never a program by hand. Sections: value shape x operation (round 1); operand order, function blocks, captures and `var self` receivers (round 3); branch merges (`merge_*`, `mergesrc_*`), multi-argument call results (`pick_*`, `pickview_*`) and direct closure calls (`clocall_*`, `clocap_*`) (round 5).
- `cargo test -q --release -p ruxen_core --test it loan_matrix -- --ignored` checks the verdicts in process: every conflict rejected unless listed in `LOAN_MATRIX_ACCEPTED_CONFLICTS`, every dead row accepted.
- `memrun.py` is the memory proof: after `cargo build --release --bins` it compiles every program, skips the rejected ones and runs the rest under Guard Malloc (macOS) or an ASan+UBSan runtime (`--checker asan`, the Linux default). It exits 1 on any crash, non-zero exit, memory-checker report, wrong `.expect` output or compiler crash; leaks are printed, not fatal (`--leaks` adds `leaks --atExit` on macOS). `--results FILE` keeps one line per program. The `loan-matrix-memory` job in `.github/workflows/pr-ready.yml` runs both checks.
